lines.en: One hour later...
: Mother — I apologize for the intrusion...
: But I would like to talk about what transpired here today if you have a moment or two to spare.
: Hm...Well at least it’s actually you this time. So how could I refuse if my oldest daughter is asking?
: You’ve refused me many times before, Mother.
: In fact, you were refusing me quite unabashedly just an hour ago when I was attempting to drag my teacher out of the devious scenario you forced him into this time.
: You seemed quite happy to be involved in that scenario until your sister tried to steal your man from under your nose, dear.
: I swear — I’m always so surprised by how reluctant you are to take the things you’re entitled to.
: No one is entitled to Sensei, Mother. Not me. Not you. And most definitely not Tsukasa.
: No wonder he sees you as a mother if you’re going to defend him like that. But you seem to be misunderstanding something, dear.
: What happened in my office was not an attempt to force your beloved Akira into anything at all. I’m just trying to do what’s best for our family.
: Well, I struggle to understand just what you believe you are doing for this family by asking the man I’ve grown a fondness for to teach both my sister and me about...sex.
: You don’t need to hesitate when using that word around me, Touka. You’re at the age now where I’m surprised you can think about anything else at all.
: I tend to keep my family out of such fantasies, thank you very much. And even if I am of that age, Tsukasa isn’t.
: She is, though. And do you want to know why she is, Touka?
: Not particularly...but if I had to wager a guess, I assume it may have something to do with the fact that you’re moving forward with this archaic tradition of marrying her off.
: Which, with all due respect, I am very disappointed to hear. For I had assumed that-
: Did you or did you not create an opportunity for your teacher and his subordinate to venture off for some “alone time” during the Christmas party, Touka?
: I...that-
: Why? Because I understand kindness, but not the type that involves sending my man off to bed another woman in my own home.
: It...is not up to me who Sensei-
: Do you know where he went with her, Touka? Would you like to wager a guess in regard to that as well?
: I...assume one of the guest rooms or a...restroom, perhaps? But does the room really-
: He went to your sister’s room.
: Then...Then he likely didn’t know it was-
: He’s been there before for her studies. And he went there on purpose that night.
: So it wouldn’t be a stretch to believe that she may have witnessed something that sparked this sudden curiosity that night, do you?
: R...Regardless of how such curiosity is founded, the fact remains that your actions today have done nothing but exaggerate it.
: Tsukasa is likely just confused by the idea that she may soon need to marry a man she hasn’t met.
: And I have to say, Mother, I’m surprised she knows at all. You’re typically better at keeping secrets than that.
: I am, aren’t I? Yet both of you have managed to figure it out on your own. So either the two of you are very smart, or I’m just getting sloppy.
: Or you’re sowing the seeds of chaos for your own amusement out of jealousy that I have managed to find something that you never could.
: Which is?
: Love for someone that was not chosen for me.
: And I imagine that’s why you’re going to ship Tsukasa off as well...so that she can’t find the same thing.
: Is that really what you think of me, Touka?
: That I’m just jealous?
: That I’ve never found love of my own before?
: I am saying that is how it appears...And with how secretive essentially all of your decision-making is, I can’t say I should be blamed for coming to such a conclusion.
: If I am to take over for this family, isn’t it time that you stop keeping me in the dark? Have I not proven to you that I am mature enough to hear the truth yet?
: Just speak to me! Stop making me guess!
: Mature. You won’t even fuck the man you love because you’re nervous about it and you want to talk about being “mature.” Give me a break.
: If it were just me in that room, I may take this bait...But Tsukasa was there as well.
: And there is simply no way that someone as smart as you would ever think that such a thing is a “good” idea. So you need to be doing it on purpose.
: You are the one creating an opportunity this time. Not me. And in your very own house too.
: You make me very proud sometimes, Touka. You really do.
: How unfortunate that this is one of those times.
: Yes...how unfortunate, indeed. I can’t imagine there’s anything I could say right now that would make you want to join me for a bath, is there?
: Not at the moment, no. I came here for the express purpose of asking you to leave Sensei alone — and to sever all of his ties with Tsukasa immediately.
: Is that for his sake? Or hers?
: You seem quite interested in your sister all of a sudden, Touka. You’ve never expressed this much concern for her before. At least not to me. So perhaps you’re the jealous one?
: Or perhaps all three of us are jealous of one another? It isn’t often we have such a handsome young man roaming around the manor. Of course we’d think things. Want things.
: But what if this goes a little deeper than that? What if there’s another possibility for what’s really going on here that I simply...can’t tell you regardless of how much I may want to?
: What if what I’m doing right now is the ultimate sign of love?
: I’m hard pressed to believe that Tsukasa’s sexual education plays any part in that at all.
: It does if he fucks her, dear.
: Mother?!!!?!?
: Tsukasa figured things out without being told and has yet to speak to me about it. She’s accepted her duty as a member of the family and is inclined to let things play out without interfering.
: I swear, she’s such a good girl when she isn’t tormenting the staff. Which is precisely why we both know she isn’t going to just ask to go against the family’s wishes.
: That’s not enough, though. If I call the wedding off without reason, that reflects negatively upon us and threatens to disrupt the ecosystem this family has fought so hard to build.
: It won’t just be her in jeopardy, it will be all of us.
: But if a third party interferes...and she falls for someone outside of our direct sphere of influence, perhaps we won’t need to call off a wedding at all?
: Perhaps no one will want one in the first place.
: Then you intend to...give her to Sensei so you don’t have to give her to someone else?! That’s your master plan?!
: Maybe. Or maybe it’s just one more lie that’s far easier for you to understand than an even harsher truth.
: I just...I understand what you mean and...I don’t want her married off at this age either. But surely there must be a way that doesn’t involve her sleeping with my teacher?
: The two of them could be married, I suppose. Lord knows being married doesn’t mean a couple is having sex. But if they wanted to, it wouldn’t be our place to stop them.
: Could she not just...marry one of the staff instead? Why does it have to be him? That’s the part I’m not understanding.
: You understand, Touka. You just don’t want to.
: The two of you want the same thing. So what’s a mother to do when that happens? Especially a mother who’s already promised to protect him as well.
: There’s only one way to save all of you. And I imagine we’ll all wind up sleeping with him eventually, so what’s the point in holding back now?
: What do you mean you made a promise to “protect him?” Because, last I checked, you’re the one constantly putting him in danger.
: So you get upset when your sister speaks of fucking him, but not me. Our bond really is a special one, isn’t it?
: Who is Sensei to you? Why must he be so intrinsically involved in everything?
: Just a friend, of course. Any other connection is purely coincidental.
: And I’m just supposed to believe that?
: No. But you’re supposed to accept it. Such is the life of a Tsukioka.

: If I had known this would be the life I’m meant to lead, I’d have offered myself up instead of Tsukasa and tried my luck elsewhere. I’m not exactly fond of treating people like pieces on a chess board.
: Chess is an acquired taste — like wine. No one starts off liking it, but you grow to appreciate its complexities in time. And eventually, it’s hard to live without it.
: Then perhaps you’ve drunk a bit too much as your movements are suddenly sloppy and unfitting of the woman I am modeled after.
: If you think you can handle this better than I can, feel free. I have no qualms with handing over the reins if you’ve come up with your own idea on how to preserve this family.
: That said, however, I imagine that you’ll ultimately arrive at the same place as me.
: And soon, you’ll understand just how much easier it would be to keep an eye on him if he was just here.
: If he is here, it will be because he wants to be. Not because one of us has forced his hand.
: I don’t disagree with that at all. I’m just tired of everyone I know wanting things and never taking them. It’s all far too nostalgic.
: Then let me say this — I will find a way to make him mine. And when I do, this type of behavior will not be tolerated regardless of whether or not you are my mother.
: Aww...you really won’t share? After all I’ve given to you?
: Listen to yourself! You are a married woman! I can’t even begin to think of what Father would say if he heard any of this right now!
: You’re right. I am married.
: But we have a long history of concubines in this family...
: And if you don’t hurry up, I might be tempted to take one.
: How would that make you feel, Touka?...
: Losing your man to your mother?...
: Better or worse than losing him to Tsukasa?...
: I wonder which one of us he’d prefer?
: I’m surprised a righteous fool like you can love him at all when you already know the answer.
: Mother-
: Hurry up.
: I don’t want you becoming an obstacle as well.
Touka Tsukioka was pissed!
It wasn’t every day that someone wanted to fuck the man she- well, actually, it was. But it wasn’t every day that her mother wanted to fuck him! And that was bad!
Or at least she thought it was bad? But similar to Akira, she left every serious conversation with Tsubasa wondering whether or not she’d just been played.
And maybe she had!
Or maybe she hadn’t. Because Tsubasa wasn’t feeling very ecstatic right now either.
And as she stood there in her towel for a solid five minutes, fingers massaging her eyelids as she came to terms with always being seen as the bad guy, she believed for a moment that maybe she was.
And maybe it was a bad idea to have a man who wore his impurest proclivities on his sleeves like cuff-links be the one to teach her youngest daughter about the birds and the bees.
It was pretty safe to say she was going through it. But that was a side of her that needed to stay concealed at the risk of destroying everything.
For if it didn’t, something told her that something else would be destroyed. And that something was far closer to her than that other something. Or something.
Neither one of us can tell you what it is because neither one of us knows.
We just know it’s bad and this is good. But it can’t be good if bad things don’t happen. Which makes the bad things less bad and more good.
Tsubasa Tsukioka was an excellent babysitter — and an even better business partner.
She’s doing a great job!
Her job just sucks.
Tsubasa’s affection has increased to [tsubasa_love]!
